sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗马·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the early 1990s, a block of European countries embarked on a pretty wild experiment.
sentences.zh: 20世纪90年代初，一帮欧洲国家开启了一项相当疯狂的实验。

sentences.en: They decided to get rid of all their money and replace it with a single common currency.
sentences.zh: 他们决定废除各自的货币，并用一种共同的单一货币取而代之。

sentences.en: Today, the euro is something we take for granted.
sentences.zh: 今天，欧元是我们习以为常的事物。

sentences.en: But 30 years ago, it was an extraordinary and risky idea.
sentences.zh: 但在30年前，这是一个非同寻常且充满风险的想法。

sentences.en: 12 different countries who spoke different languages with different cultures and economies,
sentences.zh: 12个说着不同语言、拥有不同文化和经济状况的各异国家，

sentences.en: all using the same paper money.
sentences.zh: 全部使用相同的纸币。

sentences.en: Nobody was sure if it would work.
sentences.zh: 没有人确信这是否行得通。

sentences.en: And yet, despite the risk, there were some really good reasons to try it.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管存在风险，尝试这么做确实有很好的理由。

sentences.en: This is Jacob Goldstein, the author of Money, the true story of a made-up thing.
sentences.zh: 我是雅各布·戈尔茨坦，《金钱：人造之物的真实历史》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Hey, Jacob.
sentences.zh: 嘿，雅各布。

sentences.en: Hi, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嗨，罗马。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the euro.
sentences.zh: 那我们来聊聊欧元吧。

sentences.en: Specifically, we're going to talk about the design of the paper money.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我们要聊聊纸币的设计。

sentences.en: But let's start with the idea of the euro itself.
sentences.zh: 但让我们先从欧元本身的构想说起。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can start that story with the fall of the Berlin Wall.
sentences.zh: 对，你可以从柏林墙的倒塌开始讲起。

sentences.en: How do you measure such an astonishing moment in history?
sentences.zh: 你如何衡量历史上如此惊天动地的时刻？

sentences.en: The East German government said tonight they were going to make more openings in the wall,
sentences.zh: 东德政府今晚宣布，他们将在墙上开辟更多的通道，

sentences.en: at least a dozen more.
sentences.zh: 至少再开辟十几个。

sentences.en: Put bulldozers right through the wall so that more people could cross to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 直接用推土机推倒围墙，以便更多人能够前往西方。

sentences.en: East Germany and West Germany had been separate countries since the end of World War II.
sentences.zh: 自二战结束以来，东德和西德一直是两个独立的国家。

sentences.en: And in 1990, Germany was about to become one country again, which was in many ways a joyous moment.
sentences.zh: 而在1990年，德国即将重新统一为一个国家，从许多方面来看，这是一个令人喜悦的时刻。

sentences.en: You know, the fall of this repressive regime in East Germany, the reunification of families and communities.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，东德压迫性政权的倒台，家庭和社区的重新团聚。

sentences.en: But in the post-war era, West Germany had become an economic powerhouse.
sentences.zh: 但在战后时期，西德已经成为一个经济强国。

sentences.en: And Europeans were afraid that a united Germany might be a little too strong.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人担心，一个统一的德国可能会过于强大。

sentences.en: Which, you know, they had some really grounded historical reasons to be worried about this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们有非常切合实际的历史理由来担心这种事情。

sentences.en: So the president of France, Francois Mitterrand, came up with a plan.
sentences.zh: 于是时任法国总统弗朗索瓦·密特朗想出了一个计划。

sentences.en: He proposed this deal with the German chancellor.
sentences.zh: 他向德国总理提出了这笔交易。

sentences.en: He said, we will support a reunified Germany if you, Germany, agree to give up your national currency
sentences.zh: 他说，如果我们支持一个统一的德国，前提是你（德国）同意放弃你的国家货币，

sentences.en: and join with your neighbors in this new shared money.
sentences.zh: 并与邻国一同使用这种新的共享货币。

sentences.en: Basically, he wanted to put Germany in this big European bear hug.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他是想把德国纳入这个巨大的欧洲熊抱之中。

sentences.en: And Germany said yes.
sentences.zh: 而德国答应了。

sentences.en: Because who doesn't love a bear hug?
sentences.zh: 因为谁不喜欢熊抱呢？

sentences.en: Sure, especially a European bear hug.
sentences.zh: 当然，尤其是欧洲熊抱。

sentences.en: And creating the euro involved all kinds of decisions.
sentences.zh: 而创造欧元涉及各种各样的决定。

sentences.en: Like, how do you replace all the money in the ATM machines?
sentences.zh: 比如，如何替换自动取款机里的所有现金？

sentences.en: And what is the exchange rate between the old currencies and the new one?
sentences.zh: 旧货币和新货币之间的汇率是多少？

sentences.en: And there was this one seemingly small question that took up a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 还有一个看似微小却吸引了大量关注的问题。

sentences.en: What was the new money going to look like?
sentences.zh: 这新钱会长成什么样？

sentences.en: That's my favorite dilemma.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的两难困境。

sentences.en: It's a very new question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常崭新的问题。

sentences.en: It's a very hard question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Because paper money had been this kind of nationalistic thing.
sentences.zh: 因为纸币一直以来都带有一种民族主义色彩。

sentences.en: A place where a country would put pictures of their heroes and their landmarks.
sentences.zh: 这是一个国家会将他们的英雄和地标印上去的地方。

sentences.en: But the point of the euro was to transcend nationalism.
sentences.zh: 但欧元的意义在于超越民族主义。

sentences.en: To build this single, unified Europe.
sentences.zh: 建立这个单一、统一的欧洲。

sentences.en: So, if you put, say, the Reichstag on the 100 euro note and the Eiffel Tower on the 50,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你把国会大厦印在100欧元纸币上，把埃菲尔铁塔印在50欧元上，

sentences.en: the French would be like, how come the Germans got the 100 and we only got the 50?
sentences.zh: 法国人就会觉得，凭什么德国人拿了100的，而我们只有50的？

sentences.en: And then the Dutch would be like, at least you got the 50.
sentences.zh: 然后荷兰人就会说，至少你们还拿到了50的。

sentences.en: We didn't get anything on any bill.
sentences.zh: 我们什么钞票上都没印。

sentences.en: So, when the architects of the euro announced a contest to design the new banknotes,
sentences.zh: 因此，当欧元的缔造者们宣布举办新纸币设计大赛时，

sentences.en: they added a rule.
sentences.zh: 他们加了一条规则。

sentences.en: No national heroes or national symbols or national landmarks.
sentences.zh: 不得出现国家英雄、国家象征或国家地标。

sentences.en: Which doesn't leave a lot of options.
sentences.zh: 这可没剩下多少选择了。

sentences.en: Still, designers from 14 different European central banks submitted ideas.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，来自14个不同欧洲中央银行的设计师们还是提交了构想。

sentences.en: And on December 13, 1996, the head of the European Monetary Institute had a press conference
sentences.zh: 在1996年12月13日，欧洲货币管理局局长举行了一场新闻发布会，

sentences.en: to announce the winner.
sentences.zh: 来宣布获胜者。

sentences.en: We wanted first to inform the heads of state and government about this choice because this
sentences.zh: 我们首先希望将这一选择告知国家元首和政府首脑，因为这

sentences.en: is a, this choice is clearly of a symbolic, major symbolic significance.
sentences.zh: 是一个，这个选择显然具有象征意义，具有重大的象征意义。

sentences.en: The winner, he said, was an Austrian banknote designer named Robert Kalina.
sentences.zh: 他说，获胜者是一位名叫罗伯特·卡利纳的奥地利纸币设计师。

sentences.en: In the Kalina designs, there was no Eiffel Tower, no famous author or general or queen.
sentences.zh: 在卡利纳的设计中，没有埃菲尔铁塔，没有著名的作家、将军或女王。

sentences.en: Instead, Kalina chose the most inoffensive symbols imaginable.
sentences.zh: 相反，卡利纳选择了能想象到的最人畜无害的符号。

sentences.en: The design emphasizes three main architectural elements.
sentences.zh: 该设计强调了三个主要的建筑元素。

sentences.en: Windows, gateways, and bridges.
sentences.zh: 窗户、大门和桥梁。

sentences.en: The metaphors write themselves, you know, openness, connection, exactly what you want at this moment
sentences.zh: 这些隐喻不言自明，你知道的，开放、连接，这正是一个庞大的欧洲板块自罗马帝国以来

sentences.en: when a big chunk of Europe was joining together to use a single kind of money
sentences.zh: 第一次联合起来使用单一货币时，

sentences.en: for the first time since the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 你所期望的一切。

sentences.en: And for the metaphors to work, they had to make sure these inoffensive symbols
sentences.zh: 为了让这些隐喻发挥作用，他们必须确保这些无害的符号

sentences.en: didn't represent a particular country.
sentences.zh: 不代表某个特定的国家。

sentences.en: So, the pictures on the bills weren't actual windows and gateways and bridges.
sentences.zh: 所以，纸币上的图片并不是真正的窗户、大门和桥梁。

sentences.en: They were pretend bridges, imaginary gateways.
sentences.zh: 它们是假想的桥梁，想象中的大门。

sentences.en: The images on the paper money were supposed to exude European-ness,
sentences.zh: 纸币上的图像应该散发着欧洲特色，

sentences.en: but not Spanish-ness or French-ness or German-ness.
sentences.zh: 而不是西班牙特色、法国特色或德国特色。

sentences.en: Everything went fine with the windows and gateways.
sentences.zh: 窗户和大门的设计进行得很顺利。

sentences.en: The problem was the bridges.
sentences.zh: 问题出在桥梁上。

sentences.en: The person who figured out that the problem was the bridges
sentences.zh: 发现问题出在桥梁上的人，

sentences.en: was a bridge-loving British journalist named Russ Swan.
sentences.zh: 是一位热爱桥梁的英国记者，名叫罗斯·斯旺。

sentences.en: He was the editor of a magazine called Bridge Design and Engineering.
sentences.zh: 他是《桥梁设计与工程》杂志的主编。

sentences.en: I talked to him recently, and he told me that, of course, he was delighted to learn
sentences.zh: 我最近采访了他，他告诉我，得知假想的桥梁

sentences.en: that pretend bridges were going to feature prominently on Europe's new money.
sentences.zh: 将成为欧洲新货币的显着特色时，他当然感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: We are the bridge people, and they're using our thing for their thing.
sentences.zh: 我们是造桥人，而他们正在用我们的东西做他们的事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's excellent.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这太棒了。

sentences.en: So Russ figured he would do a little story for his magazine about the paper money.
sentences.zh: 所以罗斯琢磨着为他的杂志写一篇关于纸币的小报道。

sentences.en: He requested a press pack with pictures of the bills.
sentences.zh: 他索取了一份带有纸币图片的新闻资料包。

sentences.en: This was the mid-'90s.
sentences.zh: 那是90年代中期。

sentences.en: You know, the web was just getting going.
sentences.zh: 你知道，互联网才刚刚起步。

sentences.en: And the euro people sent him pictures.
sentences.zh: 欧洲货币官员给他寄去了图片。

sentences.en: The bridges on the bills go in chronological order.
sentences.zh: 纸币上的桥梁是按年代顺序排列的。

sentences.en: So, the oldest bridges are on the smallest bills.
sentences.zh: 所以，最古老的桥梁印在面值最小的纸币上。

sentences.en: It's like this little tour through architectural history.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一次微型的建筑史之旅。

sentences.en: And as Russ is looking at these pictures,
sentences.zh: 正当罗斯看着这些图片时，

sentences.en: the first thing that catches his eye is the 500-euro note,
sentences.zh: 首先吸引他眼球的是500欧元面值的纸币，

sentences.en: which is the biggest bill and the most modern bridge.
sentences.zh: 这是面值最大、也是最现代化的桥梁。

sentences.en: The 500-euro has a cable-stayed bridge.
sentences.zh: 500欧元纸币上是一座斜拉桥。

sentences.en: It's a modern-style bridge where there are these straight cables holding up most of the structure.
sentences.zh: 这是一种现代风格的桥梁，大部分结构都由这些笔直的拉索支撑着。

sentences.en: It's graphically very striking and lovely.
sentences.zh: 它的图形非常醒目且精美。

sentences.en: Again, this is supposed to be a generic example of a bridge, not a real landmark.
sentences.zh: 再次说明，这本该是一个桥梁的通用范例，而不是真实的地标。

sentences.en: But Russ noticed something wrong with this supposedly fake bridge.
sentences.zh: 但罗斯发现这座所谓的假桥有些不对劲。

sentences.en: It looked like a bridge I'd been to visit, oh, six, seven weeks earlier in northern France.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像是我在大约六、七周前去参观过的一座位于法国北部的桥。

sentences.en: It's called the Pond du Normandie, the Normandie Bridge.
sentences.zh: 它叫诺曼底大桥。

sentences.en: And I thought, you know what, I think that's the Normandie.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，你知道吗，我觉得那就是诺曼底大桥。

sentences.en: I think that's not the fictitious structure that the European Union have said it was.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那根本不是欧盟所说的虚构建筑。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of cable-stayed bridges, and they all kind of look like this.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多斜拉桥，它们看起来都长这样。

sentences.en: But underneath the bridge at the sides are these pillars.
sentences.zh: 但在桥梁下方两侧是这些桥墩。

sentences.en: And there's this one spot where you'd expect to see a pillar, but there is no pillar.
sentences.zh: 有一个地方你理应看到桥墩，但却没有桥墩。

sentences.en: And that's true for the Pond du Normandie.
sentences.zh: 诺曼底大桥确实如此。

sentences.en: And it's also true for this design.
sentences.zh: 这个设计也是如此。

sentences.en: Russ calls up the designer of the bridge, who he'd talked to for the magazine.
sentences.zh: 罗斯打电话给这座桥的设计师，他曾为杂志采访过对方。

sentences.en: And he winds up faxing him a picture of this 500-euro bill.
sentences.zh: 他顺手把这张500欧元纸币的图片传真给了对方。

sentences.en: And he came back to me within moments and said, this is my bridge.
sentences.zh: 他很快就回复我说，这就是我的桥。

sentences.en: I recognize it.
sentences.zh: 我认得它。

sentences.en: This is absolutely, positively, the bridge that I designed,
sentences.zh: 这绝对、百分之百就是我设计的桥，

sentences.en: the bridge that you and I stood on six weeks ago in northern France.
sentences.zh: 就是你和我六周前在法国北部一起站在上面的那座桥。

sentences.en: I will stand up in a court of law and swear on anything you like that this is my bridge
sentences.zh: 我愿意走上法庭，对你能想到的任何东西发誓，这就是我的桥，

sentences.en: because there are these features that are specific to this bridge.
sentences.zh: 因为这里有这座桥所独有的特征。

sentences.en: Now, of course, this made me think I found one.
sentences.zh: 当然，这让我觉得我找到了一座。

sentences.en: I wonder if I can find some more.
sentences.zh: 不知道我还能不能找到更多。

sentences.en: If you are the editor of Bridge Design and Engineering, this is your moment.
sentences.zh: 如果你是《桥梁设计与工程》杂志的主编，这就是属于你的高光时刻。

sentences.en: So over the next couple of days, Russ looked through books and old photographs
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的几天里，罗斯翻阅了书籍和老照片，

sentences.en: trying to identify the supposedly fake bridges on the other Euronotes.
sentences.zh: 试图辨认其他欧元纸币上那些所谓的假桥。

sentences.en: And right away, he saw this picture of the Rialto.
sentences.zh: 他立刻就看到了这张里亚托桥的照片。

sentences.en: It's the famous and really very beautiful bridge in the middle of Venice.
sentences.zh: 这是威尼斯市中心那座著名且非常美丽桥梁。

sentences.en: There's an arch below.
sentences.zh: 下面是一个拱门。

sentences.en: There's a parade of shops going up one side at an angle of maybe 30 degrees and down the other side at 30 degrees.
sentences.zh: 一侧是一排以大约30度角往上延伸的商店，另一侧则以30度角往下延伸。

sentences.en: So when you look at the bridge, your eye is drawn to the superstructure, to the stuff on top of the bridge,
sentences.zh: 所以当你看着这座桥时，你的目光会被吸引到上层建筑上，也就是桥面上的东西，

sentences.en: which is the walkways and the shops and so forth.
sentences.zh: 即人行道、商店等等。

sentences.en: Russ thought the masonry of the Rialto Bridge looked awfully familiar.
sentences.zh: 罗斯觉得里亚托桥的砖石结构看起来极其眼熟。

sentences.en: So he mentally removed the walkways and the shops and all the other stuff on top of the bridge itself.
sentences.zh: 于是他在脑海中移除了人行道、商店以及桥面上所有其他东西。

sentences.en: I'd realized that that was it.
sentences.zh: 我意识到就是这样。

sentences.en: That was exactly what the banknote designer had done.
sentences.zh: 这正是纸币设计师所做的事情。

sentences.en: It just, it stripped off the top and basically did a cut and paste job onto his 50 euro banknote design.
sentences.zh: 它只是，它剥离了顶部，基本上做了一个剪切粘贴的工作，用到了他的50欧元纸币设计上。

sentences.en: So now Russ had two.
sentences.zh: 所以现在罗斯找到了两个。

sentences.en: The 500 is the Pont de Normandie.
sentences.zh: 500欧元纸币上的是诺曼底大桥。

sentences.en: The 50 is the Rialto in Venice, but with the buildings removed from the top.
sentences.zh: 50欧元纸币上的是威尼斯的里亚托桥，但去掉了顶部的建筑。

sentences.en: And over the next few days, he figured out a few more.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几天里，他又找出了好几个。

sentences.en: The 100 euro note was the Pont de Neuilly, a rail and road bridge in Paris.
sentences.zh: 100欧元纸币是巴黎的讷伊桥，是一座铁路和公路两用桥。

sentences.en: The 10 euro note is a Roman aqueduct in Segovia.
sentences.zh: 10欧元纸币是塞哥维亚的古罗马引水渠。

sentences.en: And finally, there was the image on the 5 euro note.
sentences.zh: 最后，是5欧元纸币上的图案。

sentences.en: The smallest bill, the oldest bridge.
sentences.zh: 面值最小的纸币，最古老的桥梁。

sentences.en: It was a boat bridge.
sentences.zh: 那是一座浮桥。

sentences.en: So it's not really a structure in its own right.
sentences.zh: 所以它本身并不是一个真正的建筑结构。

sentences.en: It's a series of boats with planks across them.
sentences.zh: 它是一系列上面铺着木板的船只。

sentences.en: A very ancient way of crossing a river.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常古老的过河方式。

sentences.en: This is one of my favorite choices.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的选择之一。

sentences.en: It's this like lovely old proto bridge, more than a bridge itself.
sentences.zh: 这就像这座可爱古老的原始桥梁，与其说它是一座桥，

sentences.en: It's just a, like, it's a would-be bridge.
sentences.zh: 不如说它是一个准桥梁。

sentences.en: Clever, right?
sentences.zh: 很聪明，对吧？

sentences.en: Really clever in a really kind of low-tech way.
sentences.zh: 以一种非常低科技的方式展现出真正的聪明才智。

sentences.en: So a few days into his quest,
sentences.zh: 所以在他的探索之旅开始几天后，

sentences.en: Russ found an engraving that matched the picture on that 5 euro note.
sentences.zh: 罗斯找到了一张雕刻图案，和那张5欧元纸币上的图片对上了。

sentences.en: And it was an engraving of an ancient structure in India.
sentences.zh: 那是印度一座古代建筑的雕刻图案。

sentences.en: So it wasn't even a European bridge.
sentences.zh: 所以它根本不是什么欧洲的桥。

sentences.en: Yeah, the bonus points, right?
sentences.zh: 对，还能加分是吧？

sentences.en: It's both not, not real, and it's not in Europe.
sentences.zh: 它既是假的、不是真的，而且也不在欧洲。

sentences.en: So now Russ had all these different bridges he'd identified.
sentences.zh: 所以现在罗斯把所有这些他认出来的桥都找齐了。

sentences.en: He tried to call the banknote designer, Kalina, but couldn't reach him.
sentences.zh: 他试图联系纸币设计者卡利纳，但没能联系上。

sentences.en: And he decided it was time to tell the world that these fake bridges were not fake.
sentences.zh: 于是他觉得是时候向全世界宣布，这些假桥其实并不是假的了。

sentences.en: They were fake, fake bridges.
sentences.zh: 它们是假上加假的桥。

sentences.en: So I wrote up the story for the magazine.
sentences.zh: 所以我为杂志写了这篇报道。

sentences.en: The magazine was about to go to press.
sentences.zh: 杂志当时正准备付印。

sentences.en: He pitched the story to the BBC's main TV news show, and they wanted to do it.
sentences.zh: 他把这个故事推介给了英国广播公司（BBC）的主打电视新闻节目，他们很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So they asked me to come down to London and appear on the show that night, which was all very exciting.
sentences.zh: 于是他们邀请我当晚去伦敦上节目，这让人感觉非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Who doesn't want to be on TV?
sentences.zh: 谁不想上电视呢？

sentences.en: And Russ Swan, the man who'll send the designers of the European banknotes back to the drawing board.
sentences.zh: 还有罗斯·斯旺，这个把欧洲纸币设计者们逼得要重新回图纸前修改的人。

sentences.en: We hope he's with us now.
sentences.zh: 我们希望他现在正和我们在一起。

sentences.en: Now, this was the first one.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是第一座。

sentences.en: This is the one that you spotted first of all.
sentences.zh: 这就是你最先发现的那座。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: This is the Pond of Normandy, which is a very well-known bridge.
sentences.zh: 这是诺曼底桥，这是一座非常著名的桥。

sentences.en: Opened only two years ago in France.
sentences.zh: 在法国仅仅两年前才开通。

sentences.en: The next day, my phone was ringing off the hook.
sentences.zh: 第二天，我的电话铃声就响个不停。

sentences.en: I got page one lead in the Wall Street Journal.
sentences.zh: 我在《华尔街日报》的头版头条登了出去。

sentences.en: It was in newspapers in Finland, in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 芬兰和巴西的报纸上也都有报道。

sentences.en: I was briefly almost famous and enjoyed every moment of it.
sentences.zh: 我有那么一小会儿几乎成了名人，并且享受了其中的每一个瞬间。

sentences.en: It was quite fun.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: It was fun for Russ Swan, but I can't imagine it was fun for Robert Kalina, who designed the bells.
sentences.zh: 对罗斯·斯旺来说这很有趣，但我很难想象对设计了这些纸币的罗伯特·卡利纳来说会有多有趣。

sentences.en: Kalina seemed to take it OK.
sentences.zh: 卡利纳似乎觉得还好。

sentences.en: He basically said in interviews, I thought the bridges were generic enough, but apparently not.
sentences.zh: 他在采访中基本上是说，我以为这些桥已经够大众化了，但显然并不是。

sentences.en: Kalina had to start all over again.
sentences.zh: 卡利纳不得不一切从头再来。

sentences.en: His job was to turn the fake, fake bridges into real fake bridges.
sentences.zh: 他的工作就是把那些“假假桥”变成“真正的假桥”。

sentences.en: Kalina and the Europeans, they actually consulted with engineers to make sure that they were plausible fake bridges.
sentences.zh: 卡利纳和欧洲官员们实际上咨询了工程师，以确保这些是像模像样的假桥。

sentences.en: And in fact, the bills wound up changing a lot.
sentences.zh: 事实上，纸币最终改动了很多。

sentences.en: Like, if we look at the before and after of that 500 euro note, you can see on the old 500 note, there was the missing pillar.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我们对比一下那张500欧元纸币的新旧版本，你会发现旧版500元纸币上少了一个桥墩。

sentences.en: That was the dead giveaway that it was a real bridge.
sentences.zh: 那就是它是座真桥的绝对铁证。

sentences.en: The new version has that pillar, and it really looks like a fake bridge.
sentences.zh: 新版本加上了那个桥墩，看起来真的很像一座假桥。

sentences.en: And then, maybe most interesting, on the five euro note, Kalina got rid of that boat bridge altogether and replaced it with a apparently generic Roman aqueduct.
sentences.zh: 然后，也许最有趣的是，在5欧元纸币上，卡利纳干脆去掉了那个船桥，换成了一个显然很普通罗马输水渡槽。

sentences.en: They went through all the banknote designs.
sentences.zh: 他们把所有的纸币设计都过了一遍。

sentences.en: They fixed the money.
sentences.zh: 他们把钱给修复了。

sentences.en: But the question is, did the euro actually achieve its high-minded ideals that it was trying to achieve?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，欧元真的实现了它试图达到的那些高尚理想吗？

sentences.en: Like, did it really bring Europe together?
sentences.zh: 比如说，它真的把欧洲凝聚在一起了吗？

sentences.en: At first, it did.
sentences.zh: 起初是的。

sentences.en: At first, everybody loved the euro.
sentences.zh: 起初每个人都爱欧元。

sentences.en: It really did feel like one Europe coming together in a common currency.
sentences.zh: 它真的让人感觉整个欧洲通过一种共同的货币凝聚在了一起。

sentences.en: But the new money ultimately couldn't paper over the economic differences between the different countries in Europe.
sentences.zh: 但新货币最终还是无法掩盖欧洲各国的经济差异。

sentences.en: And that really became clear after the financial crisis of 2008.
sentences.zh: 在2008年金融危机之后，这一点变得尤为明显。

sentences.en: Some countries, like Germany, recovered fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 一些国家，比如德国，恢复得相当快。

sentences.en: But other countries, like Spain and Greece, did not.
sentences.zh: 但其他国家，比如西班牙和希腊，却没有。

sentences.en: Tonight, a country deeply divided.
sentences.zh: 今晚，一个深度分裂的国家。

sentences.en: All week, the banks closed.
sentences.zh: 整个星期，银行都在关门。

sentences.en: Life savings locked up inside.
sentences.zh: 毕生积蓄被锁在里面。

sentences.en: Endless lines at ATMs.
sentences.zh: 自动取款机前排着无尽的长队。

sentences.en: And if Spain and Greece had still had their own money at that time, they could have printed more of it.
sentences.zh: 如果当时西班牙和希腊仍然拥有自己的货币，它们本可以印更多的钱。

sentences.en: They could have increased the supply of pesetas and drachmas to help their economies recover.
sentences.zh: 它们本可以增加比塞塔和德拉克马的供应量来帮助经济复苏。

sentences.en: But they'd given up that power when they joined the euro.
sentences.zh: 但它们在加入欧元区时放弃了这项权力。

sentences.en: So their economies just got worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 所以它们的经济只能变得越来越糟。

sentences.en: They wound up limping along for years.
sentences.zh: 它们最终蹒跚挣扎了多年。

sentences.en: And there is a good argument that the euro itself made them worse off.
sentences.zh: 有一个很有说服力的观点是，欧元本身让它们的处境变得更糟了。

sentences.en: Yeah, like you could make a generic European bridge for a generic European currency.
sentences.zh: 对，就像你可以为一种泛欧货币造一座泛欧桥一样。

sentences.en: But you can't make an actually generic Europe.
sentences.zh: 但你没法造出一个真正泛欧的欧洲。

sentences.en: It is many countries with lots of different issues and with lots of different economies.
sentences.zh: 它是由许多国家组成的，有着各种各样的问题和不同的经济状况。

sentences.en: Yeah, the dream of the euro was this kind of abstract theoretical idea of a connected Europe.
sentences.zh: 对，欧元的梦想是一种抽象的理论构想，关于一个互联互通的欧洲。

sentences.en: But I think maybe they should have kept those original euro designs.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得也许他们应该保留那些最初的欧元设计。

sentences.en: The ones with the pictures of real bridges to remind themselves that Europeans don't live in some abstract Europe with pretend bridges.
sentences.zh: 那些印有真实桥梁图片的版本，好提醒自己欧洲人并不是生活在某种带着假桥的抽象欧洲里。

sentences.en: They cross real bridges to real countries.
sentences.zh: 他们穿梭于通往真实国家的真实桥梁上。

sentences.en: But there's one more twist to this real bridge, fake bridge story.
sentences.zh: 不过，这个真桥假桥的故事还有一个意想不到的转折。

sentences.en: It comes in 2013 when a designer in the Netherlands convinced a town called Spakenissa to build tiny replicas of the fake bridges on the euro notes.
sentences.zh: 事情发生在2013年，当时荷兰的一位设计师说服了一个叫斯派克尼斯（Spijkenisse）的小镇，去建造欧元纸币上那些假桥的微缩复制品。

sentences.en: So let's recap.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来回顾一下。

sentences.en: It started with the desire to have fake European bridges.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于想要拥有欧洲假桥的愿望。

sentences.en: They ended up to be real fake European bridges.
sentences.zh: 结果它们成了真正的欧洲假桥。

sentences.en: And then they made an effort to make them actually fake, fake European bridges.
sentences.zh: 然后他们努力让它们变成了真正的“假桥”。

sentences.en: And now those fake European bridges are real bridges that exist in a little town outside of Rotterdam.
sentences.zh: 而现在，那些欧洲假桥成了真实存在的桥，就座落在鹿特丹郊外的一个小镇上。

sentences.en: But they're like so small, they seem like miniature golf course bridges.
sentences.zh: 但它们太小了，看起来就像迷你高尔夫球场的桥。

sentences.en: So even though they're real, they seem kind of fake.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管它们是真的，但看起来又有点假。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're even the colors of the euro notes.
sentences.zh: 对，它们甚至刷成了欧元纸币的颜色。

sentences.en: So they're not even pretending to be real.
sentences.zh: 所以它们甚至都没有假装自己是真的。

sentences.en: Yeah, the fakest real bridges ever.
sentences.zh: 对，这是史上最假的真桥了。

sentences.en: More Money Talk with Jacob Goldstein after this.
sentences.zh: 广告之后，请继续收听雅各布·戈德斯坦主持的《金钱谈话》。

sentences.en: So we're back with Jacob Goldstein.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来，我是雅各布·戈德斯坦。

sentences.en: And you authored a new book called Money, the True Story of a Made-Up Thing.
sentences.zh: 你写了一本新书，叫做《金钱：一个虚构之物的真实历史》。

sentences.en: I've read this book.
sentences.zh: 这本书我读过。

sentences.en: I've also listened to this book and read this book.
sentences.zh: 我既听过这本书，也读过这本书。

sentences.en: That's how much I loved this book.
sentences.zh: 可见我有多喜欢这本书。

sentences.en: And so I figured, you know, while you were here, just like tell us another story about money.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，既然你来了，不如给我们讲另一个关于金钱的故事吧。

sentences.en: Okay, well, let's do another paper money story.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们讲一个纸币的故事。

sentences.en: We're here talking about paper money.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里聊的正是纸币。

sentences.en: And the origin of paper money is a really interesting story that, to be honest, I didn't know before I was working on the book.
sentences.zh: 纸币的起源是一个非常有趣的故事，老实说，在写这本书之前我并不知道。

sentences.en: I'd been covering money for years, but the origin of paper money was new to me.
sentences.zh: 我报道金融多年，但纸币的起源对我来说还是新鲜事。

sentences.en: And so that story takes place in China around the year 1000 A.D.
sentences.zh: 这个故事发生在公元1000年左右的中国。

sentences.en: It happens in the province of Sichuan.
sentences.zh: 故事发生在四川省。

sentences.en: And at that time in Sichuan, they were using iron coins for money.
sentences.zh: 当时在四川，他们使用的是铁币作为货币。

sentences.en: And iron is a bad thing to use for money because it's not worth very much, right?
sentences.zh: 用铁做货币可不是什么好事，因为它很不值钱，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's heavy.
sentences.zh: 对，它太重了。

sentences.en: So like you needed a pound and a half of iron coins to buy a pound of salt, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你得用一斤半的铁币去买一斤盐，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like you have to go grocery shopping with pennies or something.
sentences.zh: 这就好比你得带着一堆硬币去杂货店买东西一样。

sentences.en: It's just bad.
sentences.zh: 这实在太糟了。

sentences.en: It's just bad kind of money.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种糟糕的货币。

sentences.en: And so this merchant in Sichuan at some point starts saying to people, look, you leave your terrible iron money with me.
sentences.zh: 所以四川的一位商人有天开始对人们说：听着，你们把你们那糟糕的铁币留在我这。

sentences.en: And I'll give you a receipt, like a claim check.
sentences.zh: 我会给你一张收据，就像存物凭证一样。

sentences.en: Roman left a thousand iron coins at my shop.
sentences.zh: 罗曼在我的店里存了一千枚铁币。

sentences.en: And you can probably see what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 你大概能猜到接下来会发生什么了。

sentences.en: Then all of a sudden, these actual like bank notes that are notes from banks saying how much money you have become the thing that people trade.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，这些实际上就像是来自银行、记录你拥有多少钱的纸币，成了人们用来交易的东西。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: They turn into money.
sentences.zh: 它们变成了货币。

sentences.en: And in fact, for a really long time, until the 20th century, paper money will be a claim check for metal, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，在很长的一段时间里，直到20世纪，纸币本质上都是金属的兑换券，对吧？

sentences.en: More often silver or gold.
sentences.zh: 通常是白银或黄金。

sentences.en: But this idea that what paper money is is a receipt and that the thing that it is representing is silver or gold persists for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 但这种观念——即纸币只是一张收据，它所代表的东西是白银或黄金——持续了非常长的时间。

sentences.en: And in China, you know, it starts with these private merchants, but then the government gets involved.
sentences.zh: 在中国，你知道的，这始于这些私人商人，但后来政府也介入了。

sentences.en: They see that it's working well.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这很管用。

sentences.en: The government takes over the business of printing paper money.
sentences.zh: 政府接管了印刷纸币的业务。

sentences.en: And there is this real flourishing in China around this time connected to and driven in part by the paper money.
sentences.zh: 大约在这个时期，中国出现了一次真正的繁荣，这与纸币有关，并在一定程度上由纸币推动。

sentences.en: You see more trade and you see science and you see urbanization enabled in part by the increased trade.
sentences.zh: 你会看到更多的贸易，看到科学的发展，看到部分由于贸易增加而实现的城市化。

sentences.en: You know, like there's like this whole restaurant scene springs up and you have cities of a million people in China, which is like 10x the size of European cities at that time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像整个餐饮业蓬勃发展，中国出现了拥有百万人口的城市，这大约是当时欧洲城市规模的10倍。

sentences.en: And this persists for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了数百年的时间。

sentences.en: Eventually, they actually try money not backed by metal.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们甚至尝试了不以金属为后盾的货币。

sentences.en: Kublai Khan is running China.
sentences.zh: 忽必烈统治着中国。

sentences.en: He says, yeah, there's still going to be paper money, but you actually cannot trade in your paper for metal, for bronze.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，纸币依然会有，但你们实际上不能再把纸币兑换成金属或青铜了。

sentences.en: It was bronze coins at that time.
sentences.zh: 当时用的是青铜币。

sentences.en: And it worked.
sentences.zh: 而且这成功了。

sentences.en: Like they had fiat money in China, you know, hundreds of years before there was any paper money at all in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 就像他们在西方根本没有任何纸币的几百年前，就已经在中国有了法定纸币一样。

sentences.en: Really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 真的很了不起。

sentences.en: So what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么后来怎么了？

sentences.en: Let me tell you.
sentences.zh: 我来告诉你。

sentences.en: There is a rebellion and the rebellion forces the Khans out of China.
sentences.zh: 发生了一场叛乱，这场叛乱迫使忽必烈家族退出了中国。

sentences.en: And there is this new dynasty, the Ming dynasty, that is basically reactionary, we would say today.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一个新的朝代，即明朝，用我们今天的话说，它基本上是带有反动性质的。

sentences.en: They don't like this paper money and all of this trade and all these cities.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢这种纸币、所有的贸易和那些城市。

sentences.en: Like the ideal for the Ming dynasty rulers is the self-sufficient agricultural village.
sentences.zh: 就像明朝统治者的理想是自给自足的农业村庄一样。

sentences.en: And they actually wind up getting rid of paper money.
sentences.zh: 结果他们最终废除了纸币。

sentences.en: This real breakthrough that, you know, helped people live better material lives disappears.
sentences.zh: 这种曾经帮助人们过上更好物质生活的重大突破就这样消失了。

sentences.en: And so for a while, there is no paper money anywhere in the world anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以在一段时间里，世界上任何地方都不再有纸币了。

sentences.en: There's a few hundred years where paper money has just gone from the face of the earth.
sentences.zh: 有几百年时间，纸币在地球上销声匿迹了。

sentences.en: And then it appears in Europe a few hundred years later.
sentences.zh: 然后几百年后，它又在欧洲出现了。

sentences.en: And in fact, after they get rid of paper money in China, China gets poorer.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在中国废除纸币之后，中国变得更穷了。

sentences.en: You know, they'd had this economic flourishing and then they get rid of it and they become worse off.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们曾有过这种经济繁荣，然后废除了它，处境就变差了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: You know, there's all kinds of stories and science fiction stories about lost technologies that people then rediscover.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有很多关于失落科技的故事和科幻小说，人们后来又重新发现了它们。

sentences.en: And it's the secret to having a great and bright future is this technology from old that's been rediscovered.
sentences.zh: 通往伟大而光明未来的秘密就是这项被重新发现的古代科技。

sentences.en: But there was this one and it was paper money and we just didn't have it out of choice for a long time.
sentences.zh: 但这就曾是其中之一，它是纸币，而我们只是在很长一段时间里出于选择而不再拥有它。

sentences.en: That's a really nice read of it.
sentences.zh: 这个解读真的很棒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like in, you know, 1500, humanity had this amazing lost technology, right?
sentences.zh: 就像在公元1500年左右，人类拥有过这种了不起的失落科技，对吧？

sentences.en: Paper money.
sentences.zh: 纸币。

sentences.en: It had sort of helped this giant society flourish for hundreds of years and then vanished from the earth.
sentences.zh: 它曾一度帮助这个庞大的社会繁荣了数百，然后却从地球上消失了。

sentences.en: Well, I love that story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我喜欢这个故事。

sentences.en: I love the whole book.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢整本书。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being here, Jacob.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你能来，雅各布。

sentences.en: Oh, thanks for having me, Roman.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢邀请我，罗曼。

sentences.en: Jacob Goldstein's book is called Money, the True Story of a Made-Up Thing.
sentences.zh: 雅各布·戈德斯坦的书叫做《金钱：一个虚构之物的真实历史》。

sentences.en: It's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 这本书棒极了。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Jacob Goldstein, edited by Chris Berube, mix and tech production by Dara Hirsch, music by our director of sound, Sean Riau.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由雅各布·戈尔茨坦制作，克里斯·贝鲁比编辑，达拉·赫施负责混音和技术制作，音乐由我们的声音总监肖恩·里奥制作。

sentences.en: Delaney Hall is the executive producer.
sentences.zh: 德兰尼·霍尔担任执行制片人。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad is the digital director.
sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔斯特ad担任数字总监。

sentences.en: The rest of the team includes Vivian Lay, Emmett Fitzgerald, Lasha Madon, Christopher Johnson, Joe Rosenberg, Sophia Klatzker, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 团队的其他成员包括薇薇安·莱、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德、拉莎·马登、克里斯托弗·约翰逊、乔·罗森伯格、索菲亚·克拉茨克，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: We are part of the Stitcher and SiriusXM podcast family, now headquartered six blocks north in the Pandora building in beautiful Uptown, Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们属于 Stitcher 和 SiriusXM 播客家族，总部现已迁往加利福尼亚州奥克兰美丽的上城潘多拉大厦，向北六个街区。

sentences.en: You can find the show and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 Facebook 上找到本节目并参与讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me at Roman Mars and the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 您可以在推特上@我 Roman Mars，或@节目 99pi.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram and Reddit too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram 和 Reddit 上。

sentences.en: You can find links to other Stitcher shows I love, as well as every past episode of 99pi at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 99pi.org 上找到我喜爱的其他 Stitcher 节目的链接，以及 99pi 过去的每一集。
